title: Hong Kong suspends Gleneagles Hospital's eHealth registration after patient app data leak
date_note: The hospital reported the incident to the eHRSS Coordinator Office and the suspension took effect on 23 November; the hospital discovered unauthorized activity on 18 November (per the release).
org: Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong (港怡醫院)
geo_basis: hospital in Hong Kong as named in the government release; city given, exact address not stated in the release
summary: Hong Kong's Health Bureau said the eHealth record sharing system (eHRSS) registration of Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong was temporarily suspended on 23 November. According to the release, unauthorized activity in the security system of the hospital's patient mobile app led to a leak of patient personal data, which the hospital discovered on 18 November. The Bureau says the app is not directly connected to eHRSS and there is no evidence eHRSS was breached.
plain: Hong Kong's health authorities have temporarily cut a private hospital's access to the shared electronic health record system after its patient app had unauthorized activity and a leak of patient personal data.
exec: A Hong Kong hospital lost access to the eHealth record sharing system after a patient app leak; the Bureau says there is no evidence eHRSS itself was breached.
action: The Health Bureau says the hospital must confirm that no medical records were leaked and submit a detailed investigation report; eHRSS access returns only after the Office confirms no unacceptable security risk.

sources.name: Hong Kong Government press release: 醫務衞生局暫時吊銷港怡醫院醫健通登記
